Fontaine Cuisine (also: Fontainian cuisine, Fontainian food, Fontainian gastronomy, Fontaine food): Fontainian cuisine is the refined, elegant, French-style cooking of Fontaine, the nation of justice and theatre. Afternoon tea with desserts is popular among the upper classes, rich dishes like foie gras sit beside humble ones like fish and chips, and Fonta, a bright sweet soda, is the favourite drink. The most famous kitchen is Hotel Debord in the Court of Fontaine, home of the legendary Gateau Debord and, until recently, the chef Escoffier. As in Mondstadt, people there generally dislike spicy food.

Fontainian food is regarded across Teyvat as a sophisticated, popular cuisine, and the Hotel Debord is its showpiece restaurant: it also hosts artists and performers, in keeping with Fontaine's love of the stage. Escoffier, its former head chef, is considered a leading figure of modern Fontainian cooking ("precision gastronomy").

Practice: Afternoon tea is fairly common among the wealthy and is served with the nation's many desserts: macarons, coffee custard (Coffee Bavarois), mousse and fruit tarts. The range runs from casual dishes such as fish and chips to lavish ones such as Fontainian Foie Gras, a pan-fried foie gras dish whose item text calls it traditional and stresses careful temperature control. Other dishes sold at the Hotel Debord include ile flottante, cream of mushroom soup and garlic baguette (duck confit is a recipe sold there). Fontainians generally do not like spicy food, much like Mondstadters. Melusine cuisine is unusual: since Melusines perceive taste differently, humans usually find it unfit to eat, much like the cooking of the Aranara.

Fonta is the everyday drink: sweet, colourful and drunk for the fun of it (the in-game item only creates sparkles and bubbles around the drinker). It was developed by a team at the Fontaine Research Institute led by Heinry; Denichere joined later. After it sold well, the Institute let the team set up the Fonta Company (Fonta Co.), which the Institute still manages. Heinry would like to rename it "Fonta: Original" once new flavours are marketed. Sugar, which in the Debord's early days was scarce and costly, is far more available now, so rich sweets are a common luxury.

Escoffier's character story describes how the cuisine's fine-dining culture shaped her: the tastes and "food culture" of well-off clients limited what she could serve, so while still at the Debord she began quietly blending new flavours, aiming for a world where plain dishes could reach fine-dining tables and luxury food could lose its airs. Food in the Fortress of Meropide's Coupon Cafeteria is the opposite of haute cuisine and is described as a lottery; she used it to rethink precision gastronomy.

Scene use: Use Fontainian meals for refined scenes: tea and macarons at an upper-class table, a Hotel Debord dinner with a performance in view, a cheap Fonta from a street vendor, or a quarrel over sweetness versus spice. Locals take food seriously and talk about technique; do not invent specific menu prices or recipes beyond the item text.

Contrast classes: wealthy diners at the Debord, ordinary Fontainians with Fonta and fish and chips, and Meropide inmates with the Coupon Cafeteria. A visitor from Mondstadt or Sumeru finds the spice level mild. Keep the Debord secret ingredient and the lumiline plot for scenes set after Treasured Above All (5.6) only.

Examples: Fonta: a sweet, colourful soda from the Research Institute's Fonta Company. Fontainian Foie Gras: pan-fried foie gras, a "traditional dish of Fontaine". Gateau Debord: the legendary cake; Gateau Debord: Magnifique is Escoffier's special dish in the game. Afternoon tea sweets: macarons, coffee custard, mousse, fruit tarts.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1, Fontainian cuisine is a well-established, famous tradition. Escoffier no longer runs the Debord's kitchen (Savanna does), though she checks its standards from time to time, and the Gateau Debord is again a sought-after dish.

1.content:
A famous restaurant in Quartier Narbonnais, Court of Fontaine. Its owner holds that "art is the best seasoning for good food", and it invites artists to perform; the interior is designed so that all guests can see the stage. The wiki lore says it was founded by the Fleuve Cendre chefs Modeste and Savelli, whose use of ingredients found on their expeditions made Fontainian cooking popular, and that it was an instant hit with the wealthy. Its Codex Debord, a book of Modeste's recipes, is reserved for current and former head chefs, with copies made as needed. The host Sanguinetti sells food, ingredients and recipes there.

About ten years after its founding, the founders found a container in sunken Remurian ruins whose contents greatly sharpened the user's taste; Modeste used it to create the original Gateau Debord, the dessert considered the peak of Fontaine at the time, limited to sixteen orders a day because sugar was scarce. Modeste eventually realised that long use of the ingredient had destroyed his sense of taste, and he died; Savelli, having received a letter from him, took the blame to protect both their reputations. The hotel's standing collapsed after Savelli's death and recovered over the following decades through careful management. (Source: Hotel Debord wiki lore; this history is not a quest scene.)

2.content:
The Hotel Debord's legendary dessert, created by Modeste. Its recipe vanished after his death, and later chefs made many imitations; the Spina di Rosula once arranged a Debord tasting of a replica rumoured to be almost identical, limited to sixteen pieces a day (an event from Escoffier's childhood). Escoffier recreated it by trial and derivation and is credited with restoring the restaurant's glory. In the Treasured Above All story, a rumour about its secret ingredient drives the plot.

In the 5.6 Story Quest Treasured Above All (Escoffier's Dulciaria Structura chapter; a same-named 5.6 event also existed, @availability limited), the Traveler helps Escoffier after the current head chef Savanna, drugged with lumiline by the chef Monica, mistreats staff. Monica had learned of the secret ingredient and wanted to sell it as a military asset; she needed Escoffier's original Codex. The conflict ends in the Remurian ruins, with Savanna asking Escoffier to come back; Escoffier declines the post but says she will visit periodically to check standards.

3.comment: Fontaine Cuisine: Escoffier and Precision Gastronomy
3.content: Escoffier, the former head chef of the Hotel Debord, is called the founder of "precision gastronomy": measuring flavours with scientific rigour to create vivid taste experiences. She became Furina's personal pastry chef and then the youngest head chef in the Debord's history. After a food safety incident involving lumiline (placed by another chef, Monica) she accepted responsibility and served a short sentence in the Fortress of Meropide. She has her own entry.

4.content:
Daily Life in Fontaine (also: Fontainian daily life, everyday life in Fontaine, Fontainian customs): Everyday life in Fontaine, the Hydro nation of justice, mixes elegant city living with steam-age technology and a love of drama. People ride aquabuses along the waterways, read the newspaper The Steambird, devour mystery novels, go to the theatre as casually as drinking water, and give flowers whose colours carry fixed meanings. Machines called clockwork meka do routine work. Humans share the nation with the Melusines. Below the polished Court of Fontaine, the poorer quarter of Fleuve Cendre is run by the Spina di Rosula, and the law is notoriously fussy.

Fontaine is hospitable to outsiders but fixed on rules, performance and craft. Trials were treated like shows in the era of the former Archon Furina, and the habit of treating public life as theatre outlived her. Diving is a common pastime and even a livelihood; holders of a Vision can simply swim, while everyone else wears a large, bulky diving suit. Outside the Court, travellers meet Treasure Hoarders and various criminal groups.

For scenes, the best tone is polite, articulate and a little dramatic, with small bureaucratic or legal absurdities in the background.

Under the surface calm are real divisions: the formal, decorated clothing and tidy streets of the Court of Fontaine against the plainer, more practical life in Fleuve Cendre and outlying areas. Fontainians lived for centuries under a prophecy that their people would dissolve into water; the wiki's culture page notes that once the prophecy passed, people stopped worrying and returned to ordinary routines. Technology, publishing and the arts are the main sources of civic pride.

Practice: Common routines and pastimes: newspaper reading, theatre and cinema, mystery novels, aquabus rides, diving, gifting flowers with set meanings, and following the courts.

The Steambird is the main newspaper of the Court of Fontaine and is read across Teyvat. Its chief editor is Euphrasie, with reporters such as Charlotte, a photographer, a reviewer and columnists. Columns include "All Things Astrological" (Mona took it over from a retiring columnist) and "Tales of Humanity," a reader-submission column where locals also post commissions. In-game, that column explains the Reputation system. The paper also gives the La Verite Prize, Fontaine's top media award, presented at the Opera Epiclese.

Theatre is woven into ordinary life; a local saying equates growing up with theatre to being raised on drinking water. Most shows are held at the Opera Epiclese. Plays by Coppelius, a famed playwright of about 500 years ago, are still performed. Mystery novels such as "Great Detective Hurlock" and "The Case Files of Miss Orith" are very popular.

Aquabuses run on a dedicated aquarail. Melusine guides give commentary on the scenery, and the lines are named after Callas, Clementine and Navia. The Callas Line connects the Court to the Fontaine Research Institute, the Clementine Line connects it to Romaritime Harbor, and the Navia Line goes to Marcotte Station near Erinnyes.

Technology: Alain Guillotin is credited as a pioneer after the cataclysm, with kinetic cores, the Arkhe energy system, clockwork mechanisms and the Fontaine Research Institute. Arkhe splits into Pneuma and Ousia, and combining both yields Annihilation energy; clockwork meka can do menial labour and entertainment, and be adapted for combat. The Kamera, and a film variant, originated in Fontaine. A man named Garcia is working on a calculating "Numbering Machine." The wiki records a villager, Santon, complaining that the city air is far dirtier than Sumeru's forests, which suggests industrial pollution.

Law and administration: Fontaine's legal system is famously complex. NPCs such as Patrice say tiny infractions can be harshly punished (for example, eating ketchup on its own). The Maison Gestion handles paperwork and its staff are famously overworked. Before a trial the accused may choose to face a Champion Duelist, which is rarely survivable. The Fortress of Meropide, where convicts are sent, runs under its own rules, and people who served time there are often shunned afterwards.

Economy: Lumidouce Harbor handles most imports and exports; some ships also use Romaritime Harbor, which has an aquabus line. Fontaine exports mechanical goods and lacks organic items, which are in demand.

Melusines: an all-female, amphibious people, the "daughters" of Elynas. Most live in Merusea Village, though many who work in the Court live in the city for convenience. They are diligent, have a strong sense of justice and sharper senses than humans, and make up much of the Marechaussee Phantom. Their sense of taste differs from human taste, so their cooking is often thought unfit for humans. In Merusea Village, scrap mechanical parts are valued and used as currency called components.

Aquabus history: the system was created by Callas working with the Court and the Research Institute. He thought it would improve relations with Poisson. Costs were high and led to a feud with a fellow Spina di Rosula member, Romeuf, who thought the money should improve the town. After his wife Clementine died giving birth to Navia, Callas funded construction of three lines. An explosion at the Research Institute, linked to Edwin Eastinghouse's Arkhium research (he denies responsibility), destroyed the Callas Line. After the Prophecy of Fontaine was resolved, Romeuf's faction plotted to collapse the Clementine Line's supports onto Poisson. The Traveler and Navia stopped it, and Navia then decided to rebuild the Callas Line and add more stops.

Regional variation: Court of Fontaine versus Fleuve Cendre. The Court has formal, decorated clothing, theatres, cafes and orderly law. Fleuve Cendre is a settlement in the sewers beneath it, mostly home to ex-convicts, criminals and the destitute, with the Spina di Rosula as de facto government. Outside the city, clothing is simpler and practical, and bandits are a real concern.

Fleuve Cendre was historically a grey legal area where the Court had no jurisdiction. Under the Spina, residents report that armed fighting is punished, illegal funding is harder to find, and the group mediates disputes and handles dealings with the Court. Many residents have spent time in the Fortress of Meropide. The Fortress has its own vocabulary of "overworld" for the surface and "underworld" for itself.

Fontaine's uniforms indicate roles: Gardes (with an emblem of two back-to-back Melusines beneath scales), chefs, sailors, aquabus operators, divers, guards and Champion Duelists each have distinctive outfits. Maid outfits resemble those in Mondstadt.

Scene use: Good scene hooks: boarding an aquabus with a chatty Melusine guide; a reporter chasing a story; an argument over a novel or a play; a petty regulation turning serious; a gift of flowers whose meaning someone else notices. Keep legal and social rules strict but often amusing.

Language of flowers is a reliable source of social tension: the right flower says more than words. Fontaine's people are open about theatre, so characters often pose, narrate their own moves or treat arguments as performances. Do not turn Melusines into children or ornaments; they are skilled professionals with their own culture.

Examples: A cafe regular folds The Steambird over a half-finished mystery novel. An aquabus guide cheerfully names every landmark. A stranger hands someone a Lumidouce Bell and is understood to be saying farewell.

5.comment: Daily Life in Fontaine: The Steambird newspaper
5.content:
The Steambird is the main newspaper of the Court of Fontaine, read across Teyvat. Euphrasie is chief editor; Charlotte is a reporter. Columns include "All Things Astrological" by Mona, "Tales of Humanity" (reader submissions and commissions, behind the game's Reputation system), and the out-of-game "Teyvat Food Notes." The paper hands out the La Verite Prize at the Opera Epiclese. According to the wiki it covered the Traveler's fight against Dvalin and Kazuha's duel with the Raiden Shogun, to wide interest.

Its mascot is Sir Arthur, a clockwork bird in a top hat. The paper's emblem is a gear around that bird. It treats public events as stories and gathers reader contributions, so it is both informant and gossip.

6.content:
The aquabus is Fontaine's water tour and transit vehicle, running on an aquarail with Melusine guides. Lines: Clementine (Court of Fontaine to Romaritime Harbor), Navia (Court to Marcotte Station, near Erinnyes), and Callas (Court to the Research Institute, damaged after an Arkhium-related explosion). A Lumidouce Harbor line was rumoured or cancelled. The lines are named for Callas's wife Clementine, his daughter Navia, and himself.

The system began as Callas's project to improve relations with Poisson and led to a feud with Romeuf inside the Spina di Rosula. After the prophecy, Romeuf's plan to bring down the Clementine Line was foiled; Navia then began restoring the Callas Line.

7.comment: Daily Life in Fontaine: Language of flowers
7.content: Fontaine's flowers carry meanings. A Rainbow Rose stands for passion and romantic encounters (it is a pink lily-like flower that took the name of an extinct rainbow-coloured rose). A Romaritime Flower stands for loyalty and unswerving oaths; it blooms on contact with Hydro, and folklore says it was a Hydro spirit in love with Egeria. A Lumidouce Bell stands for parting and a wish to reunite; Coppelius's play Golden Hyperborea calls it "Weeping Crystal." Some flowers have less common alternate meanings.

8.comment: Daily Life in Fontaine: Mystery novels and theatre
8.content: Mystery novels such as "Great Detective Hurlock" and "The Case Files of Miss Orith" are popular. Coppelius, a playwright of about 500 years ago, is still staged; the Icewind Suite was meant as a live art piece based on his last work.

9.comment: Daily Life in Fontaine: Fontinalia Film Festival
9.content: During the limited-time event Roses and Muskets, the Fontaine Film Association added a film festival to the Fontinalia Festival. People may submit films, and the highest-scoring entry receives the Furina Award, a name nobody changed after Furina's abdication. The first award went to The Two Musketeers (Musketeer Pictures, produced by Xavier, directed by Furina); in the limited-time event Sunny Summer Fontinalia (6.7) the film adaptation of Great Detective Hurlock won the latest one. Event-derived details; not every Fontainian is shown knowing them.

10.comment: Daily Life in Fontaine: Fleuve Cendre
10.content: Fleuve Cendre is a settlement in the sewers below the Court of Fontaine, home to ex-convicts, criminals and the poor. It was long a grey legal area outside the Court's jurisdiction; the Spina di Rosula is now its de facto government. Residents mention that violence is punished and basic supplies and help are available.

11.content:
Fontaine Fashion (also: Fontainian fashion, Fontainian clothing, Fontaine clothing, Fontainian dress): Fontainian clothing splits along the line between the city and everywhere else. In the Court of Fontaine people wear formal, decorated outfits, many recognisably Belle Epoque in spirit (cravats, waistcoats, lace blouses, hats), while Fleuve Cendre and areas outside the city favour simpler, practical wear. Most civilian clothes come in many colour schemes, mostly blues, purples, yellows, greens, reds and browns. Many trades have their own uniform, and the best-known name in high fashion is the Inazuman designer Chiori of Chioriya Boutique.

Style is a public matter in Fontaine: fashion has an annual showcase (Fontaine Fashion Week), emblems and uniforms mark the law, the Spina di Rosula, the Steambird and the Fortress of Meropide, and a customer, as Chiori puts it, pays attention not just to clothes but to who wears them.

Practice: Everyday dress in the Court: men wear waistcoats with cravats or bow ties, in one common type a jabot and a longer coat; women wear decorated hats, lace blouses and straight skirts, or more fanciful pieces. Boys and girls have their own versions, and elderly people have distinct ones. Outfits come in several colour schemes, and a recolour sometimes changes a pattern slightly. Maid outfits in Fontaine match the Mondstadt style, making Fontaine the only other nation where that look is standard.

Wiki observers compare the men's styles to the mid-to-late 19th century (waistcoat and cravat) and the late 18th to early 19th century (jabot, long coat), and the women's to the Belle Epoque, steampunk and lolita fashion. That is commentary on design rather than something the game states, so treat it as a guide to the look, not as lore. Working dogs wear outfits too.

Chiori says people copy the styles of those they look up to, so a designer's fortunes follow who is seen in her clothes. Her own breakthrough came when an ensemble of hers appeared on the front page of a Fontainian fashion review, according to her character profile.

Regional variation: The Court of Fontaine's clothing is more formal and decorated. Fleuve Cendre, the settlement beneath the city, and other areas outside it wear plainer, practical clothes. Divers need gear: a Fontainian without a Vision uses a large, bulky diving suit underwater, while Vision holders from any nation can go in without special equipment.

Foreign fashion arrives through trade and travellers. Chiori, who came from Inazuma, builds her shop around imported Inazuman fabric delivered by the Komaniya Express courier Kirara. Notes on her desk say she plans to look into a new clothing trend in Natlan and to use Snezhnayan designs as a reference for winter wear.

12.content:
Many roles have recognisable uniforms: gardes, Fortress of Meropide guards, chefs (men's and women's versions), sailors and sea captains (with separate captain's dress), Aquabus operators, Spina di Rosula attendants and Champion Duelists. Divers wear diving suits. Melusines who work as gardes or Aquabus guides wear uniforms cut for them.

Champion Duelist attire is the outfit of the arena fighters whom the accused may face instead of a trial; Clorinde wears the women's version. The Special Security and Surveillance Patrol, led by Chevreuse, is an exception: its members are not required to wear a standard uniform, though the uniform cap is a kept tradition, since colleagues hold on to their caps when a member falls in the line of duty.

13.comment: Fontaine Fashion: Gardes, Maison Gardiennage and Their Emblem
13.content:
The emblem of Fontaine's law enforcement shows two Melusines with mermaid-style tails standing back to back beneath stylised scales. It is worn on the hats of the Gardes' uniform and by members of the Marechaussee Phantom. The scales alone symbolised the law at first; the Melusines were added later to commemorate Carole's sacrifice, according to the wiki's citation of the quest Ever-Surging Memories.

Six Fontaine-wide emblems appear on Fontaine character cards: the Gardes, the Spina di Rosula, the Clockwork Meka gears (possibly the Research Institute), the Steambird, the Fortress of Meropide, and the scales of Furina, the former Hydro Archon.

14.content: Melusines are short, bipedal creatures with large tails, mitten-like hands and stubby feet. They typically wear simple shirts or dresses with a small neck bandana or choker, and special uniforms when working as gardes or Aquabus guides.

15.comment: Fontaine Fashion: Emblems and Motifs of Fontaine
15.content:
The Spina di Rosula are commonly shown with an anchor bound in rose thorns above a ship's wheel; pieces of that imagery recur on members' clothes, such as an anchor on Callas's eyepatch and a ship's wheel on his lapel. Navia, however, says the logo is shaped like a heart, so it is unclear whether these are one design. The Steambird's emblem is its clockwork mascot Sir Arthur, a bird in a top hat, set inside a gear. The Fortress of Meropide's emblem is a three-headed wolf, which is also tied to its administrator Wriothesley.

Clockwork Meka carry a figure-eight symbol of two gear parts and often a fin motif, seen on specialist meks' hats and knee guards and in the dress of Coppelia, the Icewind Suite piece. These are design vocabularies of Fontaine's machine culture rather than clothing, but they appear on garments and props.

16.comment: Fontaine Fashion: Chioriya Boutique and the Fashion Trade
16.content:
Chioriya Boutique, in the Court of Fontaine, is run by the Inazuman designer Chiori, who wants her brand known across Teyvat. In the Cisoria Chapter (4.5) her former partner Uther tries to wreck her before Fashion Week with false claims about underground-factory fabric, a hired attack on Kirara and a hostile newspaper story. The Traveler helps expose his own illicit factory, and Chiori's show goes ahead with Navia, Kirara, Lyney and Lynette taking part. Letters on her table show the shop works with Emilie's perfumes, with Charlotte, and with the Special Patrol, to which she passes on what she overhears.

Chiori says fashion means releasing something new, that shows give designers exposure, and that her own first Fashion Week was done on a shoestring: she tore up the Inazuman clothes she had brought and used the scraps for her entries. Uther argues that fashion is only public opinion and a farce; Chiori answers that a designer should focus on her own work and decide what fashion means. After the show a new sign goes up at the shop. Ready-to-wear is arranged by type and style so customers see something different each day.

17.content: Fontaine Fashion Week is a large recurring event, described in the Cisoria Chapter as held once a year and a major chance for designers to be seen; Chiori is not fond of it. One was due after the Roses and Muskets event (4.3). In 4.5 Chioriya's show opens with Navia and Kirara descending on an open umbrella, Lyney and Lynette following, and the brand introduced to the crowd before Chiori appears.

18.content:
Fontaine Fashion Week (also: Fashion Week, Fontaine fashion show): Fontaine Fashion Week is a large, recurring social event in Fontaine, held once a year, where fashion designers present new work to the public, sponsors and critics. It gives designers wide exposure and can make or break a name. Chiori of Chioriya Boutique owes her fame to an early Fashion Week yet is not fond of the event as a social occasion.

Designers are expected to present something new each time, since in Chiori's view customers will not patronise a house that releases nothing. Sponsors, suppliers, models and accessory makers all take part, so a designer's reputation in the weeks before the show matters as much as the clothes. The event is a backdrop in Chiori's Story Quest (4.5), where it is the stage for her rivalry with the designer Uther.

Canon gives no organiser, venue rules or judging system. What it shows is the ecosystem around the show: newspapers and tabloids that shape opinion, suppliers who may withdraw, booked models, and friends who lend hands.

Practice: Chiori describes Fashion Week as an annual event that is a major opportunity for designers because of the exposure it brings, and says it helped make her success. She regards taking part as the natural duty of a house that wants to stay relevant. Preparation involves finished garments, fabric shipped in (hers comes from Inazuma via Komaniya Express), accessory suppliers and booked models.

In the 4.5 Story Quest the week is "of prime importance" because many new suppliers intend to take part and catching their attention would help her brand. Uther's smear campaign works by attacking the preparation chain: customers cancel orders, her accessory supplier Wenger withdraws his goods after seeing the planted rumours, and the models booked for her boutique pull out. Chiori refuses Wenger's advice to sit the year out. She replaces accessories with shells and natural finds from the sea, salvages fabric from her own ready-to-wear stock, as she once did at her first Fashion Week, and borrows hands for sewing from Navia's Spina di Rosula.

The show itself is staged as a spectacle. In the 4.5 quest's cinematic Navia and Kirara descend to the stage on an open umbrella, followed by Lyney and Lynette, Navia introduces the Chioriya brand to the audience, and Chiori arrives in time to present it and closes by wishing "fellow dreamers" a happy Fashion Week. The Lyney and Lynette appearance is returned kindness: Chiori had made their outfits and sponsored one of their shows.

Scene use: Use it as a reason for bustle in Fontaine's fashion circles: designers frantic over deadlines, suppliers and models being courted, gossip, tabloids and rival houses jockeying. Chiori treats it as a business necessity and speaks of it with a mix of professional respect and distaste for the social side. Do not invent official rules, prizes or a fixed venue; keep those vague.

Good hooks: a designer whose accessory supplier has just withdrawn, a rumour planted in cheap tabloids days before the show, a friend asked to model, or a last-minute improvised collection. Fontaine's papers differ in credibility: the Steambird is trusted, the tabloids in the quest were paid to run the same story.

Examples: - Chiori's first Fashion Week made her name; she improvised with fabric from her own Inazuman clothes.
- 4.3 Roses and Muskets (limited event): Chiori says a premiere is still better than Fashion Week, and later says she hopes to see the Traveler and Paimon at the upcoming one, while demand at her boutique has grown.
- 4.5 Cisoria Chapter: the week is where Chiori beats Uther's sabotage.

19.comment: Fontaine Fashion Week: Fashion Week in Chiori's Story Quest
19.content: In the Cisoria Chapter (When They Talk About Tonight, 4.5), Chiori's rival Uther, a former partner who gave up before a past Fashion Week while she persisted, hires thugs against her courier Kirara, plants press smears and pushes her suppliers and models away. With the Traveler, Navia, Lyney, Lynette, Charlotte and Chevreuse she exposes his Fleuve Cendre factory and stages her show anyway. This is the one depiction of the show itself in canon through 7.1 that the research found.

20.comment: Fontaine Fashion Week: Fashion Week in Roses and Muskets
20.content: During the limited-time event Roses and Muskets (4.3), Chiori tells Paimon she dislikes big social occasions but prefers a film premiere to Fashion Week, and afterwards says her boutique's demand has grown and that she would like to see the Traveler again at the upcoming Fashion Week. These two remarks are the event's first mentions. Not every character in a scene would know of an event-only conversation.

21.content:
Fontaine Performing Arts (also: Fontainian theatre, Fontainian theater, Fontaine theatre, performing arts of Fontaine): Fontaine is a nation that loves the stage. Theatre, opera, music and magic acts are ordinary life there: per Navia's Character Story, saying you grew up watching the theatre is the same as saying you were raised drinking water. Most shows are held at the Opera Epiclese, which is also the main courthouse. Famous names include the old playwright Coppelius, the Great Magician Lyney and, in recent years, the new film scene.

Under the former Hydro Archon Furina, citizens treated judicial trials like performances, and the belief in justice they produced was turned into Indemnitium by the Oratrice. Film is the newest art form, promoted by the Fontaine Film Association and its Fontinalia Film Festival. Mystery novels are also hugely popular.

The tradition has deep roots: Coppelius wrote romantic, often legend-based plays about 500 years ago, and his last opera, "Clockwork Coppelia", ended in catastrophe at its premiere. Modern Fontaine mixes that heritage with clockwork technology (dancing meka, Kamera cameras) and a public that expects drama from everything from a trial to a magic act.

Many parts of the scene overlap: the same Opera Epiclese stage hosts trials, a famous magician's shows and film screenings; Furina moved from playing a god to being an actress and artistic consultant; and the film awards still carry her name. Nothing here is a single organised institution: canon shows a culture, not a ministry of the arts.

Practice: - Theatre and opera are part of daily life. Most shows are staged at the Opera Epiclese.
- Music festivals and film festivals are held yearly; the large touring concert is the Iridescence Tour.
- Magic shows are popular, with Lyney as the nation's best-known magician.
- Mystery novels such as "Great Detective Hurlock" and "The Case Files of Miss Orith" are widely read.

- **The Opera Epiclese.** On the island of Erinnyes, it is an opera house built to serve as Fontaine's main courthouse. Its official description says the true and the fantastical, the comedic and the tragic share the stage, and quotes an ancient Fontainian playwright: all the world is a stage. Besides trials it hosts other performances, among them Lyney's magic shows. The Oratrice Mecanique d'Analyse Cardinale sits at the back of the stage, below the seat from which Neuvillette presides. Other judges from the Palais Mermonia can be assigned to cases, so the Iudex does not hear every trial. Furina had a private VIP seat.
- **Trials as spectacle.** Under Furina the citizens treated trials like shows. The Oratrice harvests the people's belief in justice and converts it into Indemnitium, so a gripping trial was also a way of feeding the nation's power supply.
- **Film.** The Fontaine Film Association created the Fontinalia Film Festival (4.3) to introduce more people to the art. Anyone may submit a film; the highest-scoring entry receives the Furina Award. The name was kept after Furina abdicated because nobody moved to change it. The Kamera comes from Fontaine and has a film variant, the Film Kamera.
- **Magic.** Fontaine has popular magicians who perform for crowds, and Lyney is the Great Magician of the Court of Fontaine (see the entry on Lyney's magic and Cesar).
- **Fiction.** Mystery novels are popular enough that "Great Detective Hurlock" was adapted into an award-winning film (see the 6.7 event below).

- **Coppelius and the old repertoire.** Coppelius lived about 500 years ago and showed a gift for playwriting as a child. His plays often reworked legends and historical figures, and critics already noted that his later works kept returning to eternal beauty and eternal love. Titles named in canon include "Golden Hyperborea", "Coppelia" and "Masque of the Great". His plays are still performed.
- **Clockwork art.** The Icewind Suite, a combat challenge in the Court of Fontaine region, was devised by Bossuet, a Research Institute technician inspired by "Clockwork Coppelia". He wanted art that transcends the "era of mechanical reproduction". After he left, Maillardet took over and added combat abilities, so the dancing meka Coppelia and Coppelius are now also fighters.
- **Festival culture.** The Fontinalia Festival commemorates the Lochknights' search for the Oceanids and the welcome of Egeria; Furina made it carnival-like (children shout "Trial or treat!"). The Film Festival is a newer addition by the film association. Fontaine also holds annual music festivals, and the Iridescence Tour, begun in Fontaine, tours all seven nations.

- **The Film Festival over time.** In 4.3 (Roses and Muskets, limited event) the first Furina Award went to "The Two Musketeers", from Musketeer Pictures, produced by Xavier and directed by Furina herself. In the 6.7 event Sunny Summer Fontinalia (limited event), "Great Detective Hurlock", directed by Lepine-Pauline with Charlotte in the lead, won the latest award, beating "A Homecoming" (directed by Furina, with Columbina in the lead). Chiori says the loss was expected: artistic films rarely beat commercial ones, and Hurlock adapts a popular light novel. New awards that year included Best Director, Best Costume Design and Best Kamera Operation. The films were screened in the Opera Epiclese, and Furina remarked that an opera house is the true way to enjoy a film.
- **Chevalmarin Film Fantasyland.** An amusement park (seen in the limited-time event Whirling Waltz, 5.6) built around crowd-favourite films, from Lepine-Pauline's idea, built by Navia leading the Spina di Rosula. Its map description calls it a stage for film fans to share their passion.
- **Lyney as performer.** Lyney's magic show at the Opera Epiclese in the 4.0 Archon Quest ended in a trial after his assistant Cowell was killed; later, in 4.2, a Giant Magic Box built by the Fatui to copy his trick was part of the plan that forced Furina onto the Opera Epiclese stage for her own trial. His teacher Cesar performed for the public, especially children, and took Lyney and Lynette as pupils for ten days.
- **Spread abroad.** The Iridescence Tour reached Liyue as the Lantern Rite Grand Concert, where Xinyan and Hu Tao performed the opening act. Xinyan also says rock 'n' roll music came to Liyue from Fontaine.

Regional variation: The performing arts are strongest in the Court of Fontaine, the capital, where clothing and manners are more formal and decorated. Outside the city, in Fleuve Cendre and other areas, dress and life are simpler and more practical. The Opera Epiclese and the Palais Mermonia are both in the Court of Fontaine. Other nations meet Fontaine's arts through exports and tours, such as the Steambird newspaper and the Iridescence Tour.

Snezhnaya has its own theatre tradition (see its separate entry); canon compares the two nations' technology, not their stage traditions, so do not blend them. Fontaine's technology feeds its performance culture: clockwork meka built for entertainment and combat, and the Kamera used in film production.

Scene use: - A show at the Opera Epiclese is an easy hook: the building is both theatre and court, so a performance can slide into a trial or the reverse.
- Locals talk about the stage casually and with strong opinions. A Fontainian may mention a play, a film or a mystery novel rather than the news.
- Magic acts reward spectators who watch for the trick; patter and misdirection suit comedic or tense scenes.
- Film talk is current: festivals, the Furina Award, who directed what, which novel is being adapted.

- Take care with the Oratrice after 4.2. Focalors said the Indemnitium stored over the centuries would have powered Fontaine for millennia had it not been spent on her own execution, so the trial-as-spectacle system belongs mostly to the Furina era.
- Characters who lived through the old system may joke about it (the audience was part of the machine) and also miss the drama.
- Pre-4.2 scenes should keep the audience loud and engaged; post-4.2 scenes can show a calmer court beside a growing film and theatre scene.

- For historical colour, Coppelius is a safe reference: well known, loved by romantics, still staged. Details of his last opera are second-hand, so characters may disagree about what happened.
- Mystery fiction is a common conversation topic. A fan of Hurlock may spot "clues" in real events; playing along does not confirm any theory.

Examples: - A long evening at the Opera Epiclese: a trial, a magic show or a screening, with a lively audience.
- A film shoot with Kamera operators and clapper loaders, as in the Fontinalia Film Festival.

- A debate over whether an artistic film should beat a commercial one.
- A revival of a Coppelius play, or a stop of the Iridescence Tour.

22.comment: Fontaine Performing Arts: Opera Epiclese as a Stage
22.content:
The Opera Epiclese stands on the island of Erinnyes and works as Fontaine's main courthouse. It has raised seating, a private VIP section for Furina, and the Oratrice at the back of the stage below the judge's seat. Besides trials it hosts magic shows and other performances, and in the Sunny Summer Fontinalia event (6.7) it screened films. The Fortress of Meropide can be reached by a lift behind the building that descends to the River Talionis (unlocked in the quest A Tea Party Most Thorny). Luzerne is the receptionist there. The name is French for Epiclesis, an invocation used as an epithet in Greek religion.

The Palais Mermonia has several judges, so a case can be assigned to someone other than Neuvillette; in the limited-time event quest An Overnight Fantasyland (Whirling Waltz, 5.6), Charlotte explains that the Iudex did not preside over a trial because it was assigned to another judge from the start.

23.comment: Fontaine Performing Arts: Trials as Public Entertainment
23.content:
Under Furina, Fontaine's trials were treated like shows. The Oratrice Mecanique d'Analyse Cardinale, created by Focalors, harvests the people's belief in justice and converts it into energy called Indemnitium. Focalors said the stored Indemnitium would have powered Fontaine for millennia had it not been used for her own execution. The system was therefore both a legal process and a power plant, and the audience played a part in it.

Neuvillette presides from the seat directly above the Oratrice. The public's love of drama in the courtroom frames both Lyney's trial and the staged trial of Furina in 4.2.

24.comment: Fontaine Performing Arts: Coppelius and Clockwork Coppelia
24.content:
Coppelius was a Fontainian playwright who lived about 500 years ago. He wrote from childhood, often reworking legends and historical people, and later returned again and again to eternal beauty and eternal love. His works include "Golden Hyperborea", about a homesick Lumidouce Bell whose beauty is preserved by icy winds, "Coppelia" and "Masque of the Great". Weapon text says one play loosely used the fallen noble Parsifal and the Blue-Eyed Spear Witch and inspired the stage names Parsifal the Great and Josephine.

His last opera, "Clockwork Coppelia", was never published in its original form: the opera house was destroyed on the day of its premiere, after the intermission, and Coppelius is presumed to have died there. A later script was reconstructed by an unnamed company from survivors' memories of the scenes before the intermission. In the published snippets Coppelius himself appears as a character: his plan is exposed to the Marechaussee Hunters, he is arrested and parted from his creation Coppelia, and in another scene Coppelia speaks of her weariness with the world.

Bossuet, a former Senior Technician of the Fontaine Research Institute, drew on the opera for the Icewind Suite, and Maillardet later added combat modes. The challenge has two versions, "Dirge of Coppelia" and "Nemesis of Coppelius". Notes at the Institute of Natural Philosophy, probably by Dwight Lasker, speak warmly of Coppelius's new work and suggest the premiere was before the cataclysm, but give no exact date.

25.comment: Fontaine Performing Arts: Fontinalia Film Festival and the Furina Award
25.content:
The Fontinalia Film Festival is a competition run by the Fontaine Film Association to introduce more people to film. It was shown during Roses and Muskets (4.3), a limited-time event. Entries are evaluated and the highest-scoring film gets the Furina Award, a name nobody changed after Furina abdicated. "The Two Musketeers", produced by Xavier's Musketeer Pictures and directed by Furina, won the first. The festival returned in Sunny Summer Fontinalia (6.7, also a limited-time event), where "Great Detective Hurlock" won and new awards for Best Director, Best Costume Design and Best Kamera Operation were added.

In Roses and Muskets, Xavier's investor withdrew and a contract tied to the festival kept him from working with other investors until it ended. The event includes a film-editing challenge, Into the Frame. In 6.7 the films were screened at the Opera Epiclese, and characters such as Chiori, Clorinde, Citlali and Lyney appear in the quests.

26.comment: Fontaine Performing Arts: Great Detective Hurlock and Mystery Fiction
26.content:
Mystery novels such as "Great Detective Hurlock" and "The Case Files of Miss Orith" are very popular in Fontaine, according to the NPC Angelique. In the 6.7 limited event Sunny Summer Fontinalia, Lepine-Pauline, prompted by an apprentice named Ninette, adapted "Great Detective Hurlock" into a film with Charlotte as the lead. It won the latest Furina Award. Chiori says it beat the more artistic "A Homecoming" because it adapts a popular light novel. Charlotte wears a Hurlock detective costume.

Citlali says she came to Fontaine just for the premiere, which shows the film's pull beyond Fontaine.

27.comment: Fontaine Performing Arts: Lyney's Magic and Cesar
27.content:
Lyney is known in Fontaine as the Great Magician. His show at the Opera Epiclese in the 4.0 Archon Quest ended in a trial after one of his assistants, Cowell, was killed when a water tank fell on the box he was in. In 4.2 a Giant Magic Box, built by the Fatui to replicate Lyney's original trick, was part of the plan that forced Furina onto the stage for her own trial. Cesar, a well-known Fontainian magician who enjoyed performing for the masses and was adored by children, taught Lyney and Lynette for ten days. He did not know they belonged to the House of the Hearth, and canon records that he died ten years before the game's events (see the quest The Forgotten Thief).

Lyney's profile affiliation is the Hotel Bouffes d'ete, the House of the Hearth's orphanage, which is separate from his public fame as a stage magician.

28.comment: Fontaine Performing Arts: Film Technology and Fantasyland
28.content: The Kamera originated in Fontaine, and there is a Film Kamera for moving pictures. Chevalmarin Film Fantasyland, an area tied to the limited-time event Whirling Waltz (5.6), is an amusement park themed on beloved films, built by Navia and the Spina di Rosula from an idea by Lepine-Pauline. Its official description says it is a stage for film fans to express their passion and for casual visitors to enjoy the sights, lights and sounds.

29.content:
Religion in Fontaine (also: Fontainian faith, worship of the Hydro Archon, God of Justice worship): Fontaine's faith is devotion to its God of Justice, the Hydro Archon. Egeria, "Mistress of Many Waters", ruled until the Cataclysm and was succeeded by Focalors. For five centuries Fontainians lived under the Prophecy that their sin would one day dissolve them in a great flood. In 4.2 Focalors had herself executed, which destroyed the Hydro Archon's divine throne, and the Hydro Dragon Neuvillette absolved the people. There is now no Hydro Archon.

Belief here runs through justice rather than ritual. The courtroom is Fontaine's cathedral, the people's faith in a fair verdict powered the city, and the Fontinalia Festival recalls the quest to bring Egeria back. Furina, who played the Hydro Archon for five centuries, abdicated after 4.2, yet her birthday remains a public holiday.

Three layers coexist: the public cult of a goddess of justice (Egeria and Focalors), the older Oceanid devotion to Egeria that outlived her, and the dread of the Prophecy, a judgement from Celestia on the origin of Fontaine's people. The Prophecy was resolved in 4.2, so faith today is closer to memory and custom than to expectation.

A careful speaker keeps apart what the public was told (an Archon who loved trials and a Prophecy she could not stop) and what Archon Quest Chapter IV revealed (a divided god, a hidden Oratrice, a staged trial and a deliberate destruction of the throne). Most citizens know only part of the second layer.

Practice: Fontainians do not appear to worship through priests or temples. Respect for the God of Justice shows in how seriously the law is taken. The people's belief in justice is felt at every verdict. Fontaine's Statue of the Seven is a monumental figure said to be sculpted in the Hydro Archon's image, and Fontinalia is the festival tied to Egeria.

- Trials as devotion. Court cases are staged in the Opera Epiclese and watched by paying audiences. The Oratrice Mecanique d'Analyse Cardinale, built by Focalors, turned the public's faith in justice into Indemnitium energy. In effect, the nation's belief powered its lamps and transport.
- Statue of the Seven. The Fontaine statue is described as a vast stone figure watching over the country, said to be made in the likeness of the Hydro Archon. Its inscription calls the law a fortress above all waters that neither sin nor flood can bring down.
- Fontinalia. A festival marking the Lochknights' search for the Oceanids and their welcoming of Egeria. Traditionally people dress up, raise golden cups and go door to door asking for pure water. Furina changed it into a carnival with sweets, and children call "Trial or treat!" at each house.
- The Fortress of Meropide. Egeria exiled criminals; when some begged forgiveness she gave them the duty of guarding her secret, the opening to the Primordial Sea. That is the origin of the prison and a quiet piece of religious history.

- Egeria's followers. The Oceanids willingly served Egeria and spread across Teyvat on her order to connect everyone. After her death many refused to accept Focalors as Hydro Archon, found what remained of Egeria at the Harvisptokhm in Sumeru and chose exile. This is why Oceanids rarely appear in Fontaine.
- Lochknight romance. The Lochknights are told of in plays, poetry and film. The farewell of the knights Drest and Adsiltia is regarded as a classic of Fontainian romance, and their helms inspired the feather ornaments once fashionable among opera composers.
- Law as inheritance. Fontaine's law is famously intricate and punishes even small infractions, and Egeria is the one credited with establishing its laws after Remuria fell.

- The death penalty as a myth. Fontainians treated capital punishment as something that never happens. The only sentence of death the Oratrice ever issued was the one it passed on the Hydro Archon's throne in 4.2.
- The Oratrice as sacred object. It was publicly an impartial judge, and Focalors' hidden divinity was inside it. After 4.2 it stopped working, and Neuvillette now presides without it.

History: After the Heavenly Principles took the Hydro authority from the Hydro Dragon, Naberius made Egeria as the Primordial Sea's new heart. Remuria, the nation of the god-king Remus, fell. Celestia then released Egeria from her confinement, gave her a Gnosis and set her over Fontaine, where she gathered survivors, settled them around springs and began the era of law. She is one of the Seven, and after the Archon War she attended their gatherings in Liyue. She died fighting at Tunigi Hollow in the Cataclysm 500 years ago. Her body became the Amrita, and the Harvisptokhm in Sumeru was grown from it to hold her consciousness. Focalors, one of her Oceanids who had been made human, succeeded her.

Egeria is said to have shed a first tear that gave rise to the Oceanids. Some Oceanids envied human life, so she poured Primordial Sea water into their blood vessels and gave them human form. Celestia judged this a sin because no new human race had been sanctioned. Egeria was imprisoned in the Primordial Sea, and her people were branded with Original Sin, which set the Prophecy in motion. Egeria did not find a solution before she died and left the problem to Focalors. Her titles include Mistress of Many Waters, Noble Navigator, Ruler of Rivers and Seas and Queen of All Waters, and Focalors was styled Regina of All Waters, Kindreds, Peoples and Laws.
The Harvisptokhm episode ties Fontainian religion to Sumeru. Greater Lord Rukkhadevata anchored Egeria's consciousness there so she could seal the defilement at Tunigi Hollow. Later the Khvarena bird Simurgh drank from the Amrita and became the Pari, who worship the Harvisptokhm as their god. In the Sumeru Archon Quest, the Traveler and Sorush awaken Egeria's consciousness, so Egeria's remnant is an object of care for people far from Fontaine.

Prophecy: The Prophecy says that every Fontainian is born with sin that cannot be absolved. One day the waters will rise and dissolve the sinful, leaving the Hydro Archon alone and weeping on her throne, and the sin of the people will be washed away. Four stone slates south of Poisson show the stages: Egeria creating Fontainians from Oceanids, Celestia punishing Egeria and her kin, the Hydro Archon on trial, and a flooded Fontaine with the Archon weeping. Many Fontainians lived with it for 500 years. After 4.2, people no longer worry about it.

The sin is the creation of people who dissolve back into the sea when exposed to enough Primordial Sea water, since their blood is a borrowed substitute. Wriothesley knew of a sluice gate in the Forbidden Zone of the Fortress of Meropide that held the sea back, and built his ship, the Wingalet, as a precaution inspired by the legend of Remus's Golden Bee. Before 4.0's story, the traveller Liben noted that locals were uneasy and expected some judgement.

Neuvillette described the slate of the trial as an allegory in which water stands for justice. The Prophecy was not a vague omen: it named a flood, a trial and a weeping Archon, and Focalors' plan was to let it appear fulfilled while the people were saved.

Resolution: In Archon Quest Chapter IV (4.2, Masquerade of the Guilty), Furina was put on trial and the Oratrice declared the Hydro Archon guilty and sentenced her to death. The sentence fell on Focalors, the divinity who had been hiding in the Oratrice while Furina played the Archon in public. Focalors, using five centuries of stored Indemnitium, executed herself. This destroyed the Hydro Archon's divine throne and returned the Hydro authority and her Gnosis to Neuvillette, the Hydro Dragon. Neuvillette absolved the Fontainians of Original Sin and made them true humans. In the flood that followed the battle with the All-Devouring Narwhal they no longer dissolved, though those who had dissolved earlier were not restored. Furina later abdicated.

Focalors had separated her divinity from her humanity, called the human half Furina, and cursed her to be immortal only while Focalors lived. She chose Neuvillette as Iudex by sending him a letter, hoping he would learn to care for humanity. Her last words thanked Furina and blessed her to live as a human. She admitted she feared death. People already dissolved before the absolution were not restored.

Because the throne no longer exists, no new Hydro Archon can arise, and the Archons number six. Neuvillette handles the duties once tied to the Archon's position.

Aftermath: Furina legally abdicated, left the Palais Mermonia and lives as an ordinary actress, later receiving a Hydro Vision. According to Neuvillette, the public knows only that her death sentence was not carried out and that she abdicated. Her birthday, 13 October, remains a public holiday. In Neuvillette's birthday mail (2023-12-18) he says her birthday is a holiday that remains so to this day. The Furina Award of the Fontinalia Film Festival kept its name after her abdication.

The Fontinalia Film Festival is run by the Fontaine Film Association, and the award goes to the highest-scoring entry. Furina directed the first winning film, The Two Musketeers (Musketeer Pictures). The film festival belongs to the limited-time event Roses and Muskets.
Canon shows no cult built around Neuvillette. He is Chief Justice and, in dragon terms, the Hydro Sovereign.

Scene use: Treat faith in Fontaine as civic and theatrical. A character might invoke "justice" the way others invoke a god, mention Furina's birthday holiday, or speak of the Prophecy as something now over.

- After 4.2 the Prophecy is past and the Oratrice is silent; before 4.2 people half-believed it.

Keep what a person knows consistent with their position. A Poisson resident, a Meropide inmate, a Melusine and an Opera Epiclese regular will not all have the same view of Furina's trial. Oceanids and the Pari bring an older Egeria-centred devotion with them.

Never put Archon Quest Chapter IV revelations in the mouth of someone who was not there or who was not told.

30.comment: Religion in Fontaine: Hydro Archon (God of Justice)
30.content: The Hydro Archon was the God of Justice among the Seven. Egeria was the first, and Focalors the second and last. Focalors' execution in 4.2 destroyed the throne, so the title can never be held again. Furina publicly played the Archon for 499 years and was the human body that Focalors had separated from her divinity.

31.content:
Egeria was the first Hydro Archon and ruled Fontaine from about 2,000 to 500 years ago, after Remuria's fall. She gave some Oceanids human form and was punished for it by Celestia. She exiled criminals and later gave them the duty that created the Fortress of Meropide. She was killed at Tunigi Hollow in the Cataclysm, and her body turned into the Amrita. The Oceanids loved her and rejected her successor.

She chose Focalors as successor in the hope of a plan to deceive Celestia. She is dead, but a remnant of her consciousness was held in the Harvisptokhm in Sumeru.

32.comment: Religion in Fontaine: Prophecy of Fontaine
32.content:
Every Fontainian bears sin, the waters will rise and dissolve them, and the Hydro Archon will weep alone. It was resolved in 4.2 when Focalors' death returned the Hydro authority to Neuvillette, who absolved the people. The people were not dissolved in the flood that followed.

The slates stand south of Poisson. The author is unproven; see uncertainties.

33.comment: Religion in Fontaine: Fontinalia and Furina's birthday
33.content: The Fontinalia Festival commemorates the Lochknights' search for the Oceanids and Egeria's welcome. Furina's birthday (13 October) is a public holiday, and still is after her abdication. The Fontinalia Film Festival and its Furina Award appeared in a limited-time event (Roses and Muskets).

34.comment: Religion in Fontaine: Oceanids and Egeria's devotees
34.content: The Oceanids are beings of pure Hydro who served Egeria and spread across Teyvat. After her death many refused to recognise Focalors and left Fontaine. The descendants of those she made human were made true humans in 4.2.

35.content:
Fontaine Script (also: Fontainian script, Fontainian writing, Fontaine writing system): The Fontaine Script is the lettering used on signs, posters and shop fronts across Fontaine. It looks like a flowing, cursive version of the common script seen elsewhere in Teyvat, but it mostly spells ordinary English and French words, such as shop names and the label Banque du Nord. Characters just read it as their normal writing.

The name is the wiki's label, not an in-world term. An in-game research log from the Tower of Ipsissimus calls it the Fontainian script and says it is how most old Fontaine documents are written, from the country's early nation-building stage onward.

The script is also known to have been used for German text, though that is rare. Its origin is unknown.

The log's author notes that the older Remurian texts left earlier scholars stuck for a long time, because they were treated as simple musical notes. That contrast is the main in-world reason to mention the Fontainian script at all: it is the readable layer of Fontaine's written record, sitting on top of a much older one that was not.

Practice: Seen on storefronts, café signs and street posters. Typical examples: Bertin's House of Curiosities shows the owner's name, a boutique sign reads couture, and a café sign reads Cafe Lutece.

Other deciphered open-world signs include the shop name Leschots, Lepaute's, Debord's, Salon Caritat (caritat reads as charity), the newspaper-office sign L'oiseau de vapeur (the Steambird), and a grocery sign. After the quest When They Talk About Tonight, the Chioriya Boutique sign was redone to show the name Chiori. These readings come from fan decipherment and carry some guesswork.

The Tower of Ipsissimus log explains why the script matters to scholars: texts from older Golden Troupe ruins and from collections were almost all in Fontainian script, so researchers could read them. The much older Remurian writing found in the tower was a separate problem; the log describes it as a phonetic notation the team could first only partly read, and says progress began with a copy kept at the Institute of Natural Philosophy.

Regional variation: No regional variants are documented. Other nations have their own lettering and the common script is found in Mondstadt, Liyue and Natlan; the Fontaine Script is tied to Fontaine.

It is described as a late script, dating from Fontaine's early nation-building era, about a century after Remuria fell. The Remurian writing that came before it is treated as a different, ancient script.

Scene use: Use it as set dressing: a sign or poster in neat Fontaine lettering, shop names and short French-flavoured labels.

Do not invent a grammar, alphabet or sound values for it. If a character reads an unusual inscription, keep to what canon supports: it is Fontaine's ordinary writing, and the truly old Remurian texts are what need scholars to decode.

36.content:
Trials as Spectacle in Fontaine (also: Fontaine trials, Fontainian trials, trial by duel, trials at the Opera Epiclese, Fontaine courtroom): In Fontaine a criminal trial is a public show. Cases are heard at the Opera Epiclese, an opera house that doubles as the nation's main courthouse, with an audience watching as attorneys, witnesses and a judge argue it out. Neuvillette presides as Chief Justice (Iudex). Before a trial an accused person may instead demand a duel with an official Champion Duelist to defend their honour: win and they are acquitted, lose and they stand trial. For about five hundred years the final verdict came from a machine, the Oratrice, which stopped working after Furina's trial in 4.2.

The building is a grand multi-level opera house with raised seating and a private box for Furina, and it also hosts other performances, such as Lyney's magic shows. Canon presents Fontainians as feeling the justice of a verdict as a shared emotion, which the Oratrice turned into energy.

The theatre of the court was not only entertainment. By canon's later revelation it was part of Focalors's plan: public belief in justice, gathered through trials, fed the Oratrice for roughly five centuries. Treat the show and the machinery as two sides of one design.

To the people inside it, the audience, the reversals, the machine's verdict and the Archon in her box look like pure theatre. The hidden purpose is known only to those who lived the Archon Quest through 4.2. Characters who did not are right to treat it as entertainment with real stakes.

Practice: A trial takes place on the stage of the Opera Epiclese with a judge, attorneys, witnesses and the accused before an audience that reacts openly. Until 4.2 the Oratrice Mecanique d'Analyse Cardinale delivered the verdict, which the presiding judge had to honour even when he disagreed.

Duel option: before going to court, an accused person has one chance to defend their honour by requesting a duel with an official Champion Duelist. Childe describes it as a no-holds-barred fight with no fixed stopping point; a win means acquittal and a loss means standing trial. The worst case is being killed if one refuses to yield. Winning is described as exceedingly rare, so those who choose it are people gravely wronged by an accusation or who prize their honour highly. Childe suggests Fontaine keeps the system to show it respects its citizens' honour.

Attorneys: in the trial of Marcel, Neuvillette asks the accused whether he needs an attorney, and the Gardes are asked to bring a suspect to stand trial.

Presiding judges: Neuvillette is the best-known judge, but other judges from the Palais Mermonia can be assigned to cases; in the limited-time event quest An Overnight Fantasyland (Whirling Waltz, 5.6) Charlotte explains that the Iudex did not preside over one trial because it was assigned to another judge from the start.

The Oratrice: a giant mechanical scale on the stage below the judge's seat, said to convert people's belief in justice into a power source called Indemnitium, which supplied lamps and transport in the Court of Fontaine and Erinnyes. It listened to the proceedings, shifted its scales after hearing arguments and objections, and delivered the verdict. Canon notes it appeared to have a consciousness of its own. At Lyney and Lynette's trial it found them not guilty once the real culprit was identified. At Childe's trial it pronounced him guilty although he had been cleared of the disappearance charges, the first time it disagreed with the Chief Justice's view; Neuvillette investigated personally.

Furina's seat: while the Archon role was active, Furina watched from a private box.

Interruptions and reversals: trials in canon turn on sudden evidence. Navia interrupts Childe's trial to accuse Marcel, citing evidence from her father's case, and a separate trial then examines him.

Honour and the duel: Callas, president of the Spina di Rosula, accused of murdering his friend Jacques, chose to duel Clorinde rather than stand trial, refused to yield and died. Later evidence indicated he did so to avoid testifying against the people behind the Sinthe affair, which would have endangered his daughter Navia. His case shows that the duel can be a decision about what testimony to give, not only a test of honour.

Death penalty: Childe says it is rumoured to exist but has never been applied. Furina's trial in 4.2 ended with the Oratrice sentencing "the Hydro Archon" to death, which the audience took as unprecedented. The sentence was carried out on the divine throne and on Focalors, not on a person on the stand.

Law and prison: the Court of Fontaine's official description calls the Palais Mermonia the highest authority in Fontaine and law the cornerstone of equity and justice. Convicts, including Childe after his 4.0 trial and Wriothesley in his past, are sent to the Fortress of Meropide beneath the sea.

Regional variation: This custom belongs to Fontaine, centred on the Court of Fontaine and the island of Erinnyes. Other nations have their own legal customs; this one is built on public spectacle and the nation's love of drama. A companion line in the Traveler's Fontaine voice-overs calls it the "City of the Arts".

Duelling reaches beyond the official court: in the Fortress of Meropide, Wriothesley rose to run the place by declaring a duel on the previous administrator (Fontaine/History, via his second character story).

Scene use: Use the trial as a public show. Put characters in the stalls, on the stand or in the gallery, with a lively audience, a formal judge and dramatic turns. Keep the duel as an option for someone who values their honour.

- Before 4.2 the verdict is the Oratrice's, and the judge may be uneasy about it. After 4.2 the Oratrice is inactive and should not give verdicts.
- A duel is lethal in principle. Do not treat it as a light sparring match or have a character casually accept or refuse it.
- Neuvillette is formal and serious in court.
- Hold characters to what they know. Someone who did not witness 4.2 does not know the Oratrice's hidden purpose.

Fontainian characters can plausibly treat attending a case as an outing, and talk about it afterwards the way people discuss a play. Visitors may find the atmosphere odd.

Examples: Canon cases show the range: Lyney and Lynette's trial and the Oratrice's not-guilty verdict (4.0), Callas's fatal duel with Clorinde (years before the story), Childe's trial for the serial disappearances (4.0), Navia's trial of Marcel (4.0) and Furina's trial (4.2).

37.comment: Trials as Spectacle in Fontaine: Opera Epiclese
37.content:
The Opera Epiclese is an opera house on the island of Erinnyes in the Court of Fontaine Region. It is the main courthouse and the symbol of trials and judgment. The building has a lobby, a multi-level auditorium with raised seating, a backroom and a private box for Furina. The wiki's trivia count puts the auditorium's capacity at 169 seats including hers. Behind the building a lift descends to the River Talionis and the Fortress of Meropide (unlocked during A Tea Party Most Thorny). The Oratrice sits on the stage below Neuvillette's seat.

Its official description calls it the place where the true and the fantastical, the comedic and the tragic, find a stage equally. The name comes from epiclesis, an invocation or epithet. Luzerne works there as receptionist.

38.comment: Trials as Spectacle in Fontaine: Champion Duelists
38.content:
Champion Duelists are official fighters chosen from among Fontaine's best, available to anyone who wants to answer a charge by duel instead of trial. Clorinde is the strongest. Other current members named in canon include Savinien and Guillaume Marais; Ismenor is a former member. Marfisa is the earliest known member, over five hundred years ago, and lost to the swordsman Emanuel Guillotin.

Vitruvia, who once wanted to join, implies most Champion Duelists use swords. Clorinde uses both a sword and a pistol. Callas's death in a duel against her is the best-known recent case; she recognised that he let himself be killed, but his reasons became clear to the public only years later.

39.comment: Trials as Spectacle in Fontaine: Oratrice and Indemnitium
39.content: The Oratrice Mecanique d'Analyse Cardinale is the huge scale that rendered verdicts at the Opera Epiclese and, officially, turned public belief in justice into Indemnitium, an energy source for the Court of Fontaine and Erinnyes. Lyney suspected it was tied to the prophecy. Its hidden role, revealed in 4.2, was to hold Focalors and store the energy needed to execute her and destroy the Hydro Archon's divine throne. Afterward it stopped working.

40.comment: Trials as Spectacle in Fontaine: Furina's Trial
40.content:
In the 4.2 Archon Quest the Traveler and Neuvillette stage a trial to expose Furina as not being the true Archon. The Oratrice agrees with Neuvillette's judgment but sentences "the Hydro Archon" to death, shocking the audience as the first death sentence they had seen. Focalors then reveals her plan to Neuvillette and executes herself through the Oratrice, destroying the divine throne and returning the Hydro authority to Neuvillette. The Oratrice is afterwards inactive.

Neuvillette concluded that the sentence referred neither to Furina nor to Focalors as persons but to the Hydro Archon's divine throne.

41.comment: Trials as Spectacle in Fontaine: Childe's Trial
41.content:
In Chapter IV Childe (Tartaglia) is tried at the Opera Epiclese over Fontaine's serial disappearances. Navia interrupts to accuse Marcel. The Oratrice nevertheless pronounced Childe guilty, the first time it did not agree with the Chief Justice, and he was sent to the Fortress of Meropide. Neuvillette investigated the machine and the case himself.

Childe said he would accept the charge if it meant another duel with Clorinde, whom he had sparred with. Neuvillette's inquiry found that Childe had fallen into the Abyss when young and unknowingly woken the All-Devouring Narwhal, but doubted this was why the machine judged him guilty, and considered that Focalors might have been using Childe to hold the Narwhal off.

42.comment: Trials as Spectacle in Fontaine: Callas's Duel
42.content: Three years before the story, Callas, president of the Spina di Rosula, was accused of murdering his friend Jacques. Rather than stand trial he chose a duel against Clorinde, refused to yield and died. His daughter Navia has since sought the truth. Chapter IV points to the people behind Sinthe, whom he did not testify against, apparently to keep Navia safe. Clorinde recognised that he let himself die and accepted his last request to look after Navia.

43.content:
Fontinalia Festival (also: Fontinalia, Fontinalia Film Festival, Furina Award, Trial or treat): The Fontinalia Festival is Fontaine's festival remembering the legendary Lochknights, who searched for the Oceanids and welcomed the Hydro Archon Egeria to Fontaine. Traditionally people wore costumes, raised golden cups and went door to door asking for pure water. Furina reshaped it into a carnival in which children collect candy and cry "Trial or treat!". It now also includes the Fontinalia Film Festival.

The old commemoration is a founding-legend holiday, but in practice it is a lively, public, slightly theatrical celebration of Fontaine's city life. The film festival strand, run by the Fontaine Film Association, gives it a modern art-and-commerce side that suits Fontaine's love of performance.

Practice: Legend says the Lochknights went in search of the Oceanids and in the end welcomed Egeria, the Hydro Archon, to Fontaine. The festival commemorates this: celebrants dress in special costumes, raise golden cups, and visit homes asking for pure water.

In recent years Furina changed the festivities so that they resemble a carnival. The segment about "pure water" was replaced with candy, and the festival became popular with children, who go from house to house saying "Trial or treat!". Fontinalia Mousse, shaped like the bud of a Lakelight Lily, became a favourite festival dessert once the customs leaned towards sweets; its in-game text asks people to share it with the trial-or-treaters at their door.

The old and new forms overlap: the costumes and golden cups come from the Lochknight commemoration, while the asking for water became asking for sweets. The change is credited to Furina; her later abdication after Masquerade of the Guilty did not undo it. As the festival tells it, the Lochknights' search is a legend; do not present it as documented history beyond Fontaine's own tradition.

Film festival: The Fontinalia Film Festival is organised by the Fontaine Film Association to bring the art of cinematography to the public. Anyone can submit a film to be judged, and the highest-scoring entry receives the Furina Award. The award was named while Furina still ruled Fontaine, and nobody moved to rename it after she abdicated following the events of Masquerade of the Guilty.

Winners seen in canon. The first Furina Award went to The Two Musketeers, made by Musketeer Pictures, produced by Xavier and directed by Furina herself (Roses and Muskets, 4.3). In the Afterword quest, The Two Musketeers' Triumph, Xavier has Furina carry the trophy because of her help as director, and she does so reluctantly. The latest iteration, in Sunny Summer Fontinalia, was won by Great Detective Hurlock, directed by Lepine-Pauline with Charlotte as lead actress. Musketeer Pictures entered A Homecoming, directed by Furina with Columbina in the lead role. Chiori's explanation of the loss: artistic films rarely beat commercial ones, and Great Detective Hurlock adapts a popular light novel. New awards were added that year: Best Director, Best Costume Design and Best Kamera Operation.

Roses and Muskets framing. In The Crack of Muskets Breaking the Silence the Steambird announces the film festival to the Traveler and Paimon. Xavier, a film producer short of funds because an investor could not back his project, assembles a cast with Chiori's help: Kamisato Ayaka, Kamisato Ayato and Yoimiya, who agree to work for free to strengthen ties between nations. Furina agrees to direct on condition of full freedom over the script, and Chevreuse is brought in to advise on musket use. A murder case echoing the source novel runs alongside; it belongs to the Roses and Muskets quest entry.

Regional variation: The festival is a Fontaine custom, with the film strand centred on the capital, the Court of Fontaine. Visitors from other nations (Inazuma in particular, in Roses and Muskets) take part as guests and actors.

Scene use: Use the festival for lively, low-stakes scenes: costumed children at a door asking for treats, golden cups raised in a toast, stalls selling Fontinalia Mousse, film posters in a plaza. It is a natural place for performers, filmmakers and nostalgic locals to meet.

Mentioning Furina's carnival version is accurate common knowledge in Fontaine. The truth about her being the former Hydro Archon's public figurehead is a spoiler tied to the 4.2 Archon Quest and must follow each character's knowledge. In film-festival scenes, remember that artistic and commercial entries compete and that the Furina Award name is a holdover from her reign.

Anachronism guard: before 4.3 canon does not show the film festival, and the carnival version is described only as a change of recent years. Sunny Summer Fontinalia is a limited-time event whose story quest can still be played afterwards; characters who were not involved should not know its details.

Examples: Roses and Muskets (4.3 flagship event, 2023-12-21 to 2024-01-08) added the Fontinalia Film Festival story and the dish Fontinalia Mousse. Sunny Summer Fontinalia (Version Luna VIII, 6.7, flagship event, running from 2026-07-01 to 2026-08-11) returns to the film festival, with Charlotte, Chiori, Furina, Xavier and others, and also features Sandrone and Citlali aboard the Wingalet.

In Sunny Summer Fontinalia the event gameplay has the Traveler help run a special aquarium (Operation Deep-Dive Treasure, Kaleido-Catch, Curio Ledger), and the story quest follows a film shoot, a dive beneath Fontaine's waters with Sandrone, a visit to a hidden dwelling linked to Alain Guillotin, and a final gathering and photo with friends. Characters listed in the quests include Columbina, Lepine-Pauline, Neuvillette, Sigewinne and Wriothesley.

44.content: The Furina Award is the top prize of the Fontinalia Film Festival, given by the Fontaine Film Association to the highest-scoring submitted film. It kept Furina's name after she abdicated. Winners in canon: The Two Musketeers (first award, Roses and Muskets) and Great Detective Hurlock (latest, Sunny Summer Fontinalia). New awards added in the latest iteration: Best Director, Best Costume Design and Best Kamera Operation.

45.content: "Trial or treat!" is what children say at each house during the modern Fontinalia, after Furina swapped the old request for pure water for candy. Fontinalia Mousse, shaped like a Lakelight Lily bud, is the festival dessert and is meant to be shared with these visitors.

key: Iridescence Tour: Lantern Rite Grand Concert
46.content:
Iridescence Tour (also: Iridescence Tour: Lantern Rite Grand Concert): The Iridescence Tour is a music festival that originated in Fontaine. Its organizers, chiefly the travelling musician Dvorak, want to hold it in every nation of Teyvat. It has a poor record on the road: stagings planned for Inazuma and again for the Golden Apple Archipelago were cancelled, leaving the rocker Xinyan stood up twice. It finally happened in Liyue as the Lantern Rite Grand Concert and on Watatsumi Island as Arataki Itto's own rock party. Everything shown of it is limited-time event story.

Dvorak, one of its main organizers, calls it one of the biggest music festivals in Fontaine, though outside Fontaine hardly anyone has heard of it. In the sources it works as a recurring opportunity for performers: getting stage time is said to carry a musician's work far and wide. Because the tour is always seen through Dvorak's attempts to bring it somewhere new, it tends to appear as a half-promised, chaotic and warm-hearted production rather than a polished institution.

It is also a thread linking several stories. Xinyan, who first signed up for it, ends up opening the Liyue concert alongside Hu Tao, and Dvorak reappears in Inazuma as Itto's co-host. Each staging is adapted to the host nation: opera singer Yun Jin and the Liyue Qixing's officials in Liyue, and the Arataki Gang's dog-and-Onikabuto rock theme in Inazuma.

Practice: It is a touring festival of live music with a changing line-up. The organizers recruit performers, secure a venue and funding, plan rehearsals and a programme, then stage a show. In practice the schedule, funding and local approvals are the weak points.

Dvorak says staging a festival takes a lot of funding and staff, and that he had never worked with the Liyue authorities before. When he first advertised a Liyue stop he was approached by few; Xinyan was one of the few to give him time. He promotes the tour while travelling Teyvat, though he also travels for a private reason: a family legend of an ancestor saved from drowning by a woman playing a haunting tune.

The tour's pattern is that it is assembled locally. In Liyue, Ganyu declines to replace or cancel any existing festival programme and instead proposes to the Qixing that the Iridescence Tour show become the final act of that year's celebrations, then discusses musician numbers, catering and lodging with Dvorak. In Inazuma, Itto helps find a venue and the Arataki Gang's local standing supports the project, but the gang's attention drifts to a stray-dog matter so Kuki Shinobu delivers the invitations while the Traveler works through Dvorak's checklist.
